sources.entry: seaborn - Statistical data visualization using Matplotlib.

summary.one_liner: Seaborn is a Python statistical data visualization library built on top of matplotlib that offers a high-level interface for attractive statistical graphics.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes seaborn as a Python visualization library based on matplotlib that provides a high-level interface for drawing statistical graphics. It points to online documentation with a tutorial, example gallery, API reference, and FAQ. Installation is via PyPI (uv pip install seaborn, with an optional seaborn[stats] extra) or conda (conda-forge recommended for faster updates). The README states it requires numpy, pandas, and matplotlib, with scipy and/or statsmodels needed for some advanced statistical functions. Testing uses pytest via make test, and linting uses ruff via make lint. The README also asks users to cite the Journal of Open Source Software paper when seaborn is used in scientific publications.
notable: High-level interface on top of matplotlib for statistical graphics
Optional stats extras for scipy and statsmodels functionality
Documentation includes tutorial, example gallery, and API reference
Citable paper published in Journal of Open Source Software
caveats: Advanced statistical features need scipy and/or statsmodels installed separately or via the stats extra
The main anaconda channel lags PyPI; conda-forge updates faster
